content.value_statement: FastAPI endpoints become inconsistent when authentication, models, and status codes vary. This skill provides concise router patterns and integration steps for reliable API development.
actual_capabilities: Explains optional and required FastAPI authentication dependency patterns.
Demonstrates response models for detail and collection endpoints.
Shows appropriate creation and deletion HTTP status codes.
Defines naming placeholders for resource-based router generation.
Lists steps for router registration, models, services, and frontend integration.
limitations: The referenced assets/template.py file is not included in the package.
The skill does not provide complete CRUD handler implementations.
It does not cover validation, error responses, pagination, or detailed authorization.
Generated routers still require project-specific review and testing.

use_cases.title: Create a First Resource Router
use_cases.description: Build a clear FastAPI router with typed responses and suitable status codes.

use_cases.title: Standardize Existing API Routes
use_cases.description: Align authentication dependencies, response models, and status codes across related endpoints.

use_cases.title: Define Team Router Conventions
use_cases.description: Establish a repeatable structure for routers, models, services, and application registration.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Router
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a FastAPI router for {{resource}} with list and detail endpoints. Use Pydantic response models and explain each status code.

prompt_templates.title: Add Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Add required authentication to write routes for {{resource}}. Keep read routes public and use the project authentication dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Protecting create, update, and delete operations

prompt_templates.title: Integrate a Router
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate a {{resource}} router into {{project_path}}. Follow existing imports, service boundaries, response models, and router registration patterns.
prompt_templates.scenario: Connecting a router to an existing application

prompt_templates.title: Review Router Consistency
prompt_templates.prompt: Review {{router_file}} for authentication gaps, incorrect response models, status code errors, and inconsistent project conventions. Propose focused corrections and tests.

output_examples.input: Create a public projects router with list and detail operations.
output: A router plan with collection and item paths.
Typed response model guidance for both operations.
Registration steps for the main application.

output_examples.input: Review authentication and status codes for a task router.
output: Recommended success status codes for create and delete operations.
A focused list of corrections and required tests.

best_practices: Reuse the project's established authentication dependencies and import patterns.
Declare response models and status codes explicitly for every route.
Test authorization, validation, success responses, and error responses before integration.
anti_patterns: Do not create new authentication helpers when approved project dependencies already exist.
Do not return untyped data when a stable response model is available.
Do not register a router before reviewing paths, prefixes, tags, and dependency behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill include a complete router template?
faq.answer: No. SKILL.md references assets/template.py, but that file is not included in this package.

faq.question: Can it add authentication to routes?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes optional and required dependency patterns that must be adapted to the target project.

faq.question: Does it support response models?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates typed response models for individual resources and resource collections.

faq.question: Which HTTP status codes does it cover?
faq.answer: It shows 201 for creation and 204 for deletion.

faq.question: Will it register the router automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides integration steps, while the agent must modify and verify the target application.

faq.question: Does it replace project testing?
faq.answer: No. Every generated or revised router requires environment-specific validation, authorization checks, and automated tests.
